title: How to Store Infant Probiotics | Parent Guide
summary: Learn how to store infant probiotics, read product labels, protect single-serve powders from heat and moisture, and handle travel with care.
body_markdown:
Wondering how to store infant probiotics between uses? The practical answer starts with the product label: storage instructions can differ by formulation and packaging, so there is no single rule that applies to every probiotic. Keep the package and directions together, protect the product as instructed, and ask the manufacturer if the label is unclear. This guide explains what to check, how to handle a single-serve powder, and what to consider when you travel.


[Ask Persephone a product question](https://persephone.bio/pages/contact)


## Why do storage directions differ between infant probiotics?


“Probiotic” describes live microorganisms used in a product. It does not tell you, by itself, how that specific product should be stored. Products can differ in their strains, formulation, packaging, and directions. Those details affect the manufacturer’s storage recommendations. One product may have different directions from another, even if both are intended for infants.


For that reason, avoid relying on a general rule you saw online or on advice meant for a different product. Refrigeration is not a universal instruction, and neither is room-temperature storage. Follow the package directions for the exact product you have. If directions are missing, hard to read, or seem inconsistent across the container and website, contact the manufacturer before making a change.


There is also a difference between storing a product and preparing it for use. The label may have separate instructions for where to keep the unopened package, how to handle it after opening, and how to mix or serve it. Read each part rather than treating one storage sentence as the whole set of directions.


## What should I check on the label first?


Before you put a product away, find its storage and handling instructions. Check the original carton, container, individual sachet, and any enclosed insert. If you bought it online, compare the physical directions with the manufacturer’s current product page. Use the instructions for the exact product and age group, not an old label or a different version.


- **Temperature.** Look for a specific range or a clear instruction such as “refrigerate” or “store at room temperature.” Do not infer a temperature from the word “probiotic.”
- **Light and moisture.** See whether the directions say to keep the package dry, protected from light, or tightly closed. Retain any inner pouch or seal that is part of the packaging.
- **Opening and resealing.** Check whether the instructions change after opening and whether the container should be closed promptly.
- **Expiration or use-by date.** Locate the date and check that it remains readable. Follow any wording about using the product by that date.
- **Preparation.** Read how to mix or serve the product and whether there are restrictions about temperature or the food or liquid used.
- **Age range.** Confirm you have the formulation intended for your child’s age. Products and directions are not automatically interchangeable.


If the package is damaged, the seal is broken when it should be intact, or key directions cannot be found, pause and ask the manufacturer or your child’s pediatrician what to do. Do not guess based on a different supplement in your cabinet.


## How should I store a single-serve probiotic powder?


Single-serve packets can make it easier to portion a product, but the package instructions still determine where and how to store them. For a powder, keeping packets dry and intact is a sensible handling priority. Use the carton or pouch supplied with the product if the directions call for it, and close it as directed after taking out a packet. Avoid leaving packets loose in a damp area or where they can be crushed, torn, or mixed up with other products.


Persephone’s Bloom and Thrive products are flavorless powders packaged in single-serve stick packs. Bloom is the infant formulation for 0–12 months; Thrive is the toddler formulation for 12–36 months. Those product details do not replace the storage or preparation directions on the current package. Check the relevant product information for[Bloom for infants](https://persephone.bio/products/bloom) or[Thrive for toddlers](https://persephone.bio/products/thrive) , and follow the label that came with your product.


Handle one packet at a time. Check that it is intact before opening, then use it according to the package directions. If a packet is punctured, damp, or otherwise compromised, do not assume it is fine because it looks mostly normal. Set it aside and ask the company for product-specific guidance. Avoid transferring powder into another container unless the manufacturer explicitly recommends that approach; the original packaging carries the product identity and directions with it.


## Does an infant probiotic need to be refrigerated?


Not necessarily. Whether refrigeration is appropriate depends on the specific product and its instructions. Putting a product in the refrigerator when its label does not call for it is not a substitute for following the stated directions. Likewise, leaving a product at room temperature when its package says to refrigerate it is not a reasonable workaround.


When the instructions specify refrigeration, keep the product in the recommended conditions and return it promptly after use, as directed. Keep the package closed and protected from moisture. When instructions specify a cool, dry place instead, choose a location that meets those words. Do not place the package next to a heat source, in direct sun, or somewhere exposed to water or steam.


If you cannot locate a clear storage instruction, do not make a decision based on another brand’s advice. Check the company’s official support information or contact its customer-care team. The[U.S. Food and Drug Administration](https://www.fda.gov/) is a government source for general information about food and dietary supplements; it is not a substitute for the storage directions for an individual product.


## Where is the best place at home to keep the package?


Choose a place that matches the package instructions and makes it easy for you to keep the product clean, dry, and identifiable. A cabinet away from cooking heat, direct sunlight, and splashes may be suitable when the label calls for storage at room temperature. That is a general household example, not a replacement for a product’s directions. If the label specifies another condition, follow it.


Consider everyday household routines, too. A convenient spot should not be next to a hot appliance, in a steamy bathroom, or within a child’s reach. Keep the product in its original packaging so you can see the product name, age range, lot information, expiration date, and instructions. Do not store packets where they could be mistaken for food or another household item.


It can help to make storage part of a simple routine: put the packet back in its designated place after each use, close the carton or pouch as instructed, and keep the directions nearby. This reduces the chance of misplacing the product or mixing up infant and toddler formulations when more than one product is in the home.


## What if the package was exposed to heat, moisture, or a temperature change?


First, check what the product directions say about storage limits. If the product was briefly left somewhere outside the recommended conditions, do not assume either that it is unaffected or that it must be discarded. How to respond depends on the product and the exposure. Note what happened, how long it may have been exposed, and whether the package was open or damaged, then contact the manufacturer for guidance.


Avoid trying to solve the uncertainty by chilling, warming, drying, or mixing the product. A temperature change after the fact does not tell you whether the product was kept as directed. If the package has visible damage, has become wet, or is missing information you need, set it aside while you seek advice. When you speak with customer care, the product name and lot number can help them identify the exact item.


If your child has already taken a product and you have a concern about their health, contact your pediatrician or another qualified health professional. Questions about a product’s condition are different from questions about your child’s care, and a clinician can help with the latter.


## How should I handle probiotics while traveling?


Travel adds changes in temperature, timing, and access to your usual storage place. Before leaving, check the label for the required conditions and whether the product has any special handling instructions. Pack only what you need in its original labeled packaging, and keep the directions accessible. A separate, clean pouch can help keep packets together, but it should not expose them to heat, moisture, or conditions contrary to the label.


Do not assume a car, stroller basket, checked bag, or sunny windowsill is an acceptable place to leave a product. These locations can have conditions that are difficult to assess. If the product requires refrigeration, plan for storage that follows its instructions rather than relying on guesswork. If the directions call for another condition, use that as your guide.


For a flight or a long trip, consider contacting the manufacturer before departure if you are unsure how to keep the product within its stated storage conditions. Bring the original package so the instructions and product identity are available. If travel conditions may have taken the product outside the recommended range, ask the manufacturer what to do before using it.


## How do I store a product after opening it?


“After opening” can mean different things: opening the outer carton, opening a resealable pouch, or opening an individual packet. Look for instructions that specify which applies. Do not assume that opening a carton changes the storage requirements for every sealed packet inside, and do not assume that a packet can be saved after it has been opened. The package directions should answer those questions.


If an individual serving is intended to be used at one time, follow its directions and do not save a partly used packet unless the manufacturer says that is appropriate. A powder exposed to air, moisture, or handling may not be in the condition intended by the package instructions. When in doubt, ask before storing or using an opened serving.


Write down or photograph the storage directions if you are likely to recycle the outer carton, but keep the product’s identity and lot details available. Do not remove required labels or transfer all the product to an unlabeled jar. The packaging helps you check the age range, date, and product-specific instructions throughout use.

## What should I compare when choosing a storage routine?


The label is the source of product-specific instructions. This table is a practical reminder of the questions to ask; it does not assign storage conditions to every brand or formulation.


### A simple check before putting the product away


1. **Confirm the product.** Read the name and age range on the carton or packet. This matters when infant and toddler products are both in the home.
2. **Read the directions.** Find the storage condition and any instructions for opening, resealing, or preparation. Check the outer package and the individual container if both have directions.
3. **Look over the packaging.** Make sure the packet or container is intact and that the product name and date can still be read. If something is damaged or unclear, set it aside and contact the manufacturer.
4. **Choose the right place.** Put the package where it will stay within the conditions on the label and where it will be easy to identify. Do not leave it in a spot with conditions that are hard to control.
5. **Return it after use.** Close the outer package as directed and put it back in its designated place. Keep the instructions available for the next serving.


This short routine is useful because storage questions often arise during busy moments, not when a parent is reading the carton carefully. A consistent place and a quick check reduce the chance of confusing products or overlooking instructions. It does not need to become a complicated tracking system. If you have several supplements at home, keeping each one in its original packaging is a simple way to preserve the information you may need.


### What details should I have ready when I contact customer care?


Specific details can make it easier to get a relevant answer. Keep the product name, formulation, lot number, and expiration date available if they are printed on the packaging. Explain whether the package is sealed or opened, where it was stored, and what happened. If there was a temperature or moisture exposure, describe the location and approximate length of time rather than guessing whether the exposure was serious.


You can also explain what part of the directions is unclear. For example, ask whether the instruction applies to the outer carton or to an opened packet, or whether a packet that experienced a particular storage condition should be used. A clear question is more useful than comparing the product to another brand whose formula or packaging may be different. Follow the manufacturer's response for that product, and keep the answer with the package if it is likely to help you later.


If you are asking about your child's health rather than package handling, contact your pediatrician. Customer care can answer product and label questions, but it cannot replace individualized health guidance. When there is uncertainty, it is reasonable to pause and get the right kind of answer before continuing a routine.


Situation What to check Practical next step


Unopened product Temperature, light, moisture, and expiration instructions Keep it in the original package under the stated conditions.


Outer carton opened Whether directions change after opening and how to close the inner package Follow the package’s opening and resealing instructions.


Single-serve packet opened Whether the serving is intended for one use and any preparation directions Use it as directed; ask the manufacturer before saving an opened portion.


Travel or temperature exposure Permitted storage conditions and what to do after an excursion Describe the exposure to customer care and get product-specific advice.


Damaged or wet packaging Whether the seal or packet is intact and whether key information remains legible Set it aside and contact the manufacturer before using it.


## How do storage and product quality fit together?


Storage is one part of evaluating an infant supplement. Parents may also want to understand what the product is, which age group it is intended for, how its ingredients are described, and what evidence supports the claims being made. Clear product information makes it easier to ask focused questions rather than relying on broad promises.


Persephone describes its infant and toddler products as synbiotics: combinations of a probiotic and a prebiotic. The term “synergistic synbiotic” refers to precision-matched probiotics and prebiotics. For a plain-language overview of the company’s approach, read[Persephone’s science information](https://persephone.bio/pages/our-science) . You can also review the[product safety information](https://persephone.bio/pages/safety) and ask your pediatrician about questions specific to your child.


These are separate questions from how to store a product. A science page cannot override the current package directions, and storage advice cannot establish whether a product is appropriate for an individual child. Keep each decision grounded in the right source: the label and manufacturer for handling, and a qualified health professional for personal health guidance.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I keep all infant probiotics in the refrigerator?


No single storage rule applies to every product. Follow the directions for the specific package. If they are unclear, contact the manufacturer rather than deciding based on another product’s instructions.


### Can I store a probiotic powder in a diaper bag?


Only if the product’s directions allow the conditions it will encounter there. A bag can be exposed to heat, moisture, or direct sun, so check the label and avoid leaving the product in places where conditions may differ from the stated instructions.


### Should I throw away a packet that got warm?


Do not decide from temperature alone. Check the label, note how long and where the packet was exposed, and contact the manufacturer for advice about that product. If the packet is damaged or wet, set it aside while you ask.


### Can I put powder into a different container for convenience?


Do not transfer it unless the manufacturer says that is acceptable. Original packaging helps protect the product and keeps its name, age range, date, and directions available.


### Where can I find product-specific answers?


Start with the current package directions and the manufacturer’s official information. Persephone’s[frequently asked questions](https://persephone.bio/pages/faq) and customer-care team can help with general product questions. For advice about your child, speak with your pediatrician.

When it comes to storing infant probiotics, the most reliable routine is the one that follows the directions for the exact product you have. Keep its packaging and instructions available, and ask the manufacturer whenever a storage question is not clearly answered.
